text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Britain's leading blue-chip index defied expectations of a bloody Monday and ended with only moderate losses as bargain-hunting emerged in the wake of Friday's steep drop, dealers and strategists said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,835.0, down 30.8 points, or 0.63 percent.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index played catch-up to Friday's severe losses on Wall Street and tumbled about 4 percent in early bourse trade, but pared losses over the session to end well off early lows. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,078.60, down 74.26 points, or 1.79 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,080.55, up 2.96 points, or 0.07 percent.

PARIS - French shares closed 1.77 percent down after having lost over 3.3 percent earlier in the day on the back of a big slide on Wall Street on Friday when Paris was closed. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,870.13, down 51.71 points, or 1.77 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed lower, as the Dow Industrials' plunge on Friday hammered local shares, particularly those in the high-technology sector, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,041.10, down 284.93 points, or 1.47 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index posted its biggest decline in two months on Friday, closing down 400.83 points, or 2.43 percent, at 16,096.88 as a rise in overnight rates fueled concerns about the Hong Kong dollar. The Hang Seng index closed at 16,096.88, down 400.83 points, or 2.43 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended off their bottom levels as Wall Street opens firmer, but local stocks still finished much weaker after their earlier hit by the Dow's nearly 250 point plunge on Friday, dealers said. The all-share index closed at 7,361.3, down 78.5 points, or 1.06 percent. The all-gold index closed at 1,016.4, down 5.8 points, or 0.57 percent, while the industrial index closed at 9,049.0, down 71.9 points, or 0.79 percent.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market slowly moved away from its early lows to close 1.8 percent down as investors nervously awaited the next U.S. session after Friday's 3.1 percent dive on Wall Street. The all-ordinaries index closed at 2,618.5, down 47.7 points, or 1.79 percent.
